import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

MAX_DRIVERS = 2

def design(feats):
    # Remove near-duplicates based on correlation
    keep = set()
    correlated = set()
    for a, b, r in [
        ("IDM6", "QWK15B", 0.96), ("EEN15", "YWC15", 0.91), ("EEN15", "TJO6", -0.91),
        ("EEN15", "JNYL10P", -0.90), ("PLL7", "NCB6", 0.87), ("VHX1A", "NMJD8", -0.87),
        ("TJO6", "JNYL10P", 0.86), ("TJO6", "NMJD8", 0.84), ("TJO6", "YWC15", -0.83),
        ("EEN15", "GDM6", -0.83), ("YWC15", "JNYL10P", -0.82), ("KIE15", "CDD15", 0.81),
        ("EEN15", "MXC13", 0.80), ("JNYL10P", "GDM6", 0.80), ("JSTE5", "YSO11", -0.79),
        ("TJO6", "GDM6", 0.78), ("PLL7", "MXC13", 0.78), ("NMJD8", "JNYL10P", 0.78),
        ("NMJD8", "VDO6", -0.77), ("JSTE5", "SAHW1", 0.76)
    ]:
        if abs(r) >= 0.6:
            correlated.add(b)
    
    # Select features not in correlated pairs
    selected_features = [fid for fid in feats.ids if fid not in correlated]
    
    # Calculate effect sizes using t-test
    effects = []
    for fid in selected_features:
        col = feats.column(fid)
        y = feats.y
        x = feats.x[:, col]
        y1 = x[y == 1]
        y0 = x[y == 0]
        if len(y1) > 0 and len(y0) > 0:
            tstat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(y1, y0, equal_var=False)
            effects.append((abs(tstat), fid))
    
    # Sort by effect size and select top drivers
    effects.sort(reverse=True)
    drivers = tuple(fid for _, fid in effects[:MAX_DRIVERS])
    
    # For logistic regression, include top 5 features
    columns = tuple(fid for _, fid in effects[:5])
    
    # Check for strong correlations between top features to form products
    products = []
    for i, fid1 in enumerate(columns):
        for j, fid2 in enumerate(columns[i+1:], i+1):
            col1 = feats.column(fid1)
            col2 = feats.column(fid2)
            corr = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, col1], feats.x[:, col2])[0,1]
            if abs(corr) >= 0.6:
                products.append((fid1, fid2))
    
    # Simple weighted score: use top features with largest effect sizes
    loadings = {}
    for _, fid in effects[:min(3, len(effects))]:
        col = feats.column(fid)
        x = feats.x[:, col]
        y = feats.y
        y1 = x[y == 1]
        y0 = x[y == 0]
        if len(y1) > 0 and len(y0) > 0:
            effect_size = np.mean(y1) - np.mean(y0)
            loadings[fid] = effect_size
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=tuple(products), loadings=loadings)
